subject: chemistry

hotspots.label: Silicon wafer
hotspots.description: A silicon wafer — the famous metalloid. It has a soft metallic shine, but it is not a full metal: it is the semiconductor at the heart of computer chips.
hotspots.positionHint: The round, softly gleaming wafer at the center of the scene.
hotspots.function: Shows silicon, the metalloid that powers electronics.

hotspots.label: The metalloid staircase
hotspots.description: The glowing diagonal tiles on the table are the metalloids — a zigzag staircase dividing the metal region from the nonmetal region.
hotspots.positionHint: The diagonal line of highlighted tiles across the table section below the wafer.
hotspots.function: Shows the staircase position of the metalloid family.

hotspots.label: Semiconductor meter
hotspots.description: This meter shows where the metalloid sits on conductivity: a metal pins to the top, a nonmetal sits near the bottom, and the metalloid rests at half — the 'semi' conductor.
hotspots.positionHint: The small vertical meter beside the wafer, visible when the conductor-meter layer is on.
hotspots.function: Shows the metalloid's in-between, switchable conductivity.

visualStyleNotes: Chemistry palette, Anatomy Atelier bar: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. The silicon wafer floats centered above a table section, lit with soft neutral studio light — the wafer carries a gentle soft-specular gleam (a muted metallic read, NOT bright chrome), but no glow, no bloom, no emissive. Clean stylized product-render look, specimen-quality not cartoon. Color on the mesh is restrained: the wafer is a muted blue-grey with a soft metallic sheen, the staircase tiles carry a faint warm cast, the table tiles are paper-white. Strong saturated color is reserved entirely for the small flat hotspot dots (molecular green / amber / slate accents from the Chemistry palette). Slow auto-rotation, calm, minimal chrome.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR. Wafer: metallic ~0.4 (between the true-metal ingot at 1 and the paper tiles at 0 — the 'semi' metallic read is the whole point), roughness ~0.3, muted blue-grey. Table tiles: paper-white, metallic 0, roughness ~0.55. Conductor meter: matte graphite frame, rough ~0.6. No emissive channels anywhere — any highlight or pulse is handled by app runtime UI, not baked into the asset.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: a silicon wafer with its table position and in-between conductivity, built to be read as 'the switchable in-between family that powers electronics.' Three procedural layers, all clean primitives:

1) MAIN: one flat round wafer (cylinder radius ~0.75, height ~0.06) at the center, muted blue-grey with a soft metallic sheen (metallic ~0.4) — gleaming but clearly not chrome. A small flat notch at one edge (like a real wafer). This is the star of the scene.

2) STAIRCASE (toggleable layer): below the wafer, a flat section of periodic table (paper-white tiles, ~9 x 5). A diagonal zigzag of tiles (metalloid positions — e.g. 3rd row, then one right/down, one right/down...) glows with a faint warm cast and slight raise, tracing the staircase between the metal and nonmetal regions.

3) CONDUCTOR METER (toggleable layer): a small vertical meter (thin rounded bar, matte graphite) beside the wafer. Three markers: a full fill labeled by icon as metal, a half fill where a small sliding indicator rests — the metalloid — and a near-empty fill as nonmetal. Icons are simple shapes (a circle, a half-circle, a sliver) rather than text.

Camera: framed so the wafer is large and centered with the table slab below; auto-rotate default. Budget 6-10k triangles. Named nodes: SiliconWafer, Notch, TableSlab, StaircaseTiles, ConductorMeter, MeterIndicator. All labels are hotspot dots in the app layer; no text on the mesh.
